title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM generates device configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded), N = 200 paired intents were executed across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns. Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference = 0.02; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (predeclared primary test). An archived paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04] (reported as exploratory distinct from the preregistered confirmatory test). Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All reported numeric values, provider‑call accounting, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). However, prior work shows LLM outputs can contain mechanically detectable faults (syntax errors, topology/reachability violations, ACL/policy mistakes) that risk outages or policy breaches [1]–[3]. Generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures that pair draft generation with deterministic verification and bounded repair have been proposed and shown in constrained prototypes to reduce mechanically checkable errors in code and configuration‑like artifacts [2], [4]. Open questions include scaling verifier‑grounded workflows across heterogeneous vendor templates, the verifier cost tradeoff, and the operational effect when the same sampled draft is used for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate). Motivated by these gaps, we preregistered and ran a paired, provenance‑traced Mininet emulation study to estimate whether a deterministic verifier plus limited repair reduces the per‑intent incidence of operationally detectable policy violations.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent NetOps‑domain studies document rapid growth in LLM‑for‑NetOps research while highlighting evaluation gaps: benchmark provenance, verifier integration, and limited multi‑vendor emulation evidence [5], [6]. Prototype and cross‑domain experiments demonstrate that LLMs can draft configurations yet often introduce syntax or semantic errors; verifier‑grounded repair and GVR pipelines recur as mitigation patterns with empirical demonstrations in constrained settings (program/code generation and narrow configuration tasks) [2], [3]. Those works motivate a provenance‑traced paired evaluation with a deterministic validator inside an emulated multi‑vendor template workflow. We cite primary sources that support the claims above and use them for positioning [1]–[6].
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 prior to model calls. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the difference in probability that an intent yields zero operationally detectable policy violations under guarded (GVR) minus baseline (single‑shot LLM). Design and sampling: paired binary design with N = 200 unique intents (baseline and guarded episodes per intent), stratified across 3 vendor‑template families and 4 topology patterns (12 strata). Generation semantics and model: executions used the declared model identifier gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; that archived configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Shared_initial_candidate semantics: preregistered and executed shared_initial_candidate semantics produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused that same candidate for baseline and guarded conditions; thus any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation outcomes and the permitted verifier‑triggered repair. Validator and repair: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 tested syntax, reachability/topology constraints, and encoded ACL/policy constraints; the guarded pipeline permitted up to one verifier‑triggered repair call per intent. Budget and accounting: preregistered maximum_model_calls = 400, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Analysis plan: preregistered primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided on paired binary success indicators; report paired risk difference. As predeclared exploratory material we compute a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) and explicitly label it exploratory. Missingness and exclusions: the preregistered missingness/exclusion rules were applied; no pairs were excluded in the archived run. Full preregistration and execution manifests are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: run completed per preregistration (completed_episode_count = 400; complete_pair_count = 200). Provider audit reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 (200 shared initial generation calls + 4 repair calls) and repair stage count = 4. Paired outcomes (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 196 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline succeed), n00 = 0 (both fail). Baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired risk difference = 0.02. Preregistered primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) yields p = 0.125 (no rejection at α = 0.05). Exploratory bootstrap: archived paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) gives a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04] for the paired risk difference; per preregistration this CI is auxiliary and exploratory. Repairs and cost: four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked (repair calls = 4). Total model calls = 204 → mean model calls per intent = 1.02; mean extra calls per intent due to guarded repairs = 0.02; mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. Missingness and deviations: no pairs were excluded and no failed episodes occurred; deterministic_reconciliation passed consistency checks. Representative artifact examples (shared initial candidate, baseline and guarded responses, and validator traces) are archived under execution/responses/* and execution/scoring/* and substantiate the numeric counts reported.
sections.discussion: Confirmatory vs exploratory inference: the preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test is the study's formal confirmatory inference (p = 0.125) and therefore does not permit rejection at α = 0.05. The archived bootstrap percentile CI is an auxiliary descriptive estimator of effect magnitude; in sparse‑discordant data (n10 + n01 small) such resampling intervals can exclude zero even when an exact conditional test does not reject. Substantive interpretation: within this provenance‑traced Mininet emulation and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic validator plus a small repair budget corrected all observed mechanically detectable baseline violations at low model‑call overhead (4 repairs across 200 intents). This suggests that when a suitable deterministic verifier exists and provides localized feedback, modest repair budgets can eliminate mechanically checkable LLM faults in an emulated, template‑based setting. Limitations in scope: results are bounded to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic vendor templates, a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), and a validator limited to mechanically checkable error classes; semantic misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected. Power and prevalence: the observed baseline failure prevalence (2%) lowered power to detect small absolute improvements versus some preregistered power scenarios; the point estimate (0.02) and exploratory CI provide effect‑size context but are not confirmatory evidence of a nonzero effect at α = 0.05. Practical implication: where deterministic verification oracles exist, GVR can correct mechanically checkable faults with small additional model cost; generalization to production hardware, other models, or broader semantic correctness classes requires further work.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation (N = 200 intents, shared_initial_candidate) of a verifier‑grounded GVR pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in a provenance‑traced Mininet emulation, the preregistered confirmatory test (exact McNemar two‑sided) did not reject (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR corrected the four observed baseline policy violations at the cost of four repair calls (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), producing an artifact‑grounded paired improvement of 2 percentage points (paired risk difference = 0.02). An archived paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04] is reported only as an auxiliary descriptive interval. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that deterministic verification plus a small repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations in this emulated setting at low model‑call cost, but they do not establish production readiness nor coverage for semantic errors outside the validator. Future studies should expand verifier coverage, evaluate additional models and real vendor hardware, and increase sample sizes to better power detection of small absolute improvements.

disclosure_statement: Declared artifacts and autonomy: declared model gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; synthetic Mininet‑style harness. Preregistration: study preregistered as C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50) prior to any model calls. Initial master prompt: immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Autonomy boundary and human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, study‑selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Generation semantics and temperature: execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per pair reused by baseline and guarded; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1); the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Accounting and provenance: reported counts (N = 200, baseline successes = 196, guarded successes = 200, model calls used = 204, repair calls = 4) and analysis artifacts are recorded in the archived execution and analysis bundles (execution/* and analysis/* paths referenced in the evidence bundle). No human manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not generalize directly to production hardware or live operations.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); higher‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from validator‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements under some preregistered scenarios.
